correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=3, two integer relations prove an Apéry normal form and pairwise-distinct residues. Every gap start is a positive difference of adjacent Apéry thresholds, giving exact residue formulas and parity-dependent total. Independently, q-coin layers are (n+2)-spaced at most; only the boundary intervals can have more than n+1 gaps. The strict inequality is solved exactly. Dijkstra checks n=3..120 and independent full enumeration n=3..60 agree; coin-change DP checks n=3..28. Finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2017 triangular-semigroup paper establishes a rectangular Apéry set and a Frobenius number but not all adjacency-block starts or the long-block spectrum. The 2022 triangular-number p-Frobenius paper covers representation multiplicities and thresholds rather than maximal consecutive gap intervals. The most pertinent published source gives only isolated gaps (one-element blocks), and its full statement and proof were compared; its singleton results do not imply the new long-gap length spectrum, though its Apéry data make the total-start calculation a closer, less independent extension. Dedicated semantic checks for deserts, gap runs, exact n^2 counts and coin-layer gaps returned no dominating match. Residual generic or unindexed coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: The published 2017 Apéry rectangle makes the all-start subclaim algorithmically deducible; priority lies principally in the explicit uniform block-start and long-desert geometry, not the rectangle.
A general established theorem about coin-count layers or numerical-semigroup deserts could subsume the long-block law even if indexed under other vocabulary.
The search index cannot establish global originality; bibliographic comparison is best-knowledge, not independent certification.

value.rationale: For a well-studied free family of three consecutive triangular generators, genus and Frobenius number do not describe the arrangement of gaps. The exact all-block count, complete parametrized starts and sharp length threshold separate large deserts between consecutive coin counts from smaller within-layer gaps and reveal a parity-dependent quadratic number of components. This structural picture is meaningful across every n>=3 and is not an arbitrary finite census or an isolated small parameter improvement.
